title: Incipit: Ex Ilss. quodam Philosophi R.C. extractum
shelf_note: A 17th-century alchemical miscellany: a Latin recipe text headed 'Speculum luminum' (p.45, an older, heavily abbreviated gothic cursive), an English/Latin treatise on the one Materia citing the Turba and Morienus (p.88), and Ripley's 'Pupilla Alchymiae. Pars Practicalis' (p.132). Squarely alchemy; the 'R.C.' in the title suggests a Rosicrucian attribution. No tradition is set, though.
structure_note: There are no structure counts in the packet. None of the three sampled pages has a translation (translation is empty on all three), so a reader gets only the transcription of a mostly abbreviated Latin/English manuscript. The title 'Ex Ilss.' is almost certainly a misreading of 'Ex MSS.' (I7, moderate). The book mixes hands: p.45 is a much older gothic cursive with its own foliation (17), so this is probably a composite volume. That is not a defect, but the catalogue's single '17th Century' date undersells it.

book_verdict: A genuine alchemical manuscript miscellany. The later English/Latin hands are transcribed well (p.88, p.132). The older abbreviated gothic recipe on p.45 is not: it turns 'urine' into 'strong wine' and 'filter' into 'silence'. No sampled page is translated, and the title misreads 'MSS.' as 'Ilss.'.
